resource.name: Strategy Pressure-Tester
resource.description: Paste a strategy doc, PRD, or roadmap. Returns the five strongest objections a smart skeptic would raise (Rumelt-style diagnosis, missing tradeoffs, untested assumptions, six-month stress scenario), each anchored to the Lenny corpus.

tools.name: strategy_classify
tools.description: Deterministic. Classifies the input as strategy / roadmap / prd / mixed so downstream critique uses the right vocabulary.

signals.description: Short reasons for the classification (e.g., 'no named challenge', 'features-by-quarter pattern').

tools.name: strategy_critique
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Runs the four-pass critique (Rumelt diagnosis, missing tradeoffs, untested assumptions, six-month stress scenario) and returns five objection cards.

tools.name: strategy_rehearse
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Multi-turn rehearsal of the counter to one chosen objection. Skeptic pushes back; user argues; ends with the strategy variant that survives.

tools.name: strategy_calibration
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Compares the current critique against the prior critique for the same user. Surfaces assumptions that resolved, tradeoffs the user actually made, and the next-quarter stress scenario. Stores critique summaries locally across runs.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web version does not expose this tool. Calibration requires persisted prior critiques in the .mcpb bundle's data dir; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #2 Strategy Pressure-Tester. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. The lenny-pressure-test skill in this repo is the engine reference. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.
dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Confirm tool composition pattern (classify → critique → rehearse) matches MCP-Apps recommended flow.
Decide whether strategy_text should be stored hashed for calibration, or only the critique summary. Privacy posture in plan says default-off retention.
Engine sharing: should strategy_critique tool import directly from lenny-pressure-test skill, or duplicate the corpus-routing logic for .mcpb portability?
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: Yes. The spec encourages composable, separable tools within a single resource. The three-step flow (classify then critique then rehearse) maps cleanly to this pattern: the host can invoke each step independently or chain them, passing doc_type from strategy_classify into strategy_critique as a parameter. Tool chaining with explicit handoff values (not implicit session state) is the recommended flow.

Store the critique summary only, not the full strategy text. Strategy docs can contain confidential roadmaps; full-text retention is the highest-risk item. The calibration value comes from tracking which objection labels resolved and which the user rehearsed, not from replaying the original text. Recommended: store critique ID, timestamp, the five objection labels (not full text), and chosen_objection_index. Hash the strategy text for deduplication if needed; do not store plaintext. The MCP Apps spec has no manifest-level retention capability — the only normative hook is readOnlyHint: false on the calibration tool, which prompts the host's confirmation UI on first use. Document what is persisted in the tool description so the host can convey it.

Duplicate the corpus-routing logic for .mcpb portability. The .mcpb bundle format is self-contained; the host cannot be expected to install the lenny-pressure-test skill as a dependency. Bundle the relevant corpus chunks and routing logic directly. If the skill is updated, a bundle refresh is the update path. Portability over DRY is the right tradeoff for Phase 2. Flag the duplication with a comment in the bundle so a Phase 3 refactor can consolidate if the spec adds inter-bundle references.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
